sections.title: Choosing one thing over another
sections.content: You already met inkább ("rather, preferably") back when comparing products in a shop. It works the same way for any choice: put inkább right in front of the verb (or the word you're choosing) to say what you'd rather do. Add mint ("than"), the same word you already use for comparisons, to name the option you're passing over.

sections.title: inkább in a sentence
rows: I'd rather drink tea than coffee.

items.english: I'd rather walk than take the bus.
Tonight we'd rather have dinner at home.

sections.content: inkább...,mint... reuses the same mint you already know from comparatives — it just puts inkább in front instead of a -bb ending, because you're weighing a choice, not measuring a difference in degree.
